([[Saint George, Virginia]]) | college = * [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse]] (2022–2024) * [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]] (2024–2026) | draft_year = 2026 | draft_round = 2 | draft_pick = 44 | draft_team = [[San Antonio Spurs]] | career_start = 2026 | years1 = {{nbay|2026|start}}–present | team1 = [[San Antonio Spurs]] | years2 = [[2026–27 NBA G League season|2026]]–present | team2 = →[[Austin Spurs]] | highlights = * [[Lefty Driesell Award]] (2026) * [[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] Defensive Player of the Year (2026) * ACC Sixth Man of the Year (2026) * 2× [[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] All-Defensive Team (2024, 2026) }} '''Maliq Xavier Brown''' (born November 16, 2003) is an American [[basketball]] player for the [[San Antonio Spurs]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA), on a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Austin Spurs]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse Orange]] and [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke Blue Devils]]. == Early life == Brown was born in [[Culpeper, Virginia]] into an athletic family, and began football at age five and basketball at around age seven.{{Cite web |last=Ditota |first=Donna |date=2022-05-18 |title=Syracuse basketball recruit Maliq Brown's transformation from football star to basketball wonder |url=https://www.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/2022/05/syracuse-basketball-recruit-maliq-browns-transformation-from-football-star-to-basketball-wonder.html |access-date=2024-12-14 |website=syracuse |language=en}} He attended [[Blue Ridge School]], an independent all-boys high school in [[Saint George, Virginia|St. George, Virginia]], where he was a four-time VISAA Division II basketball state champion. Brown was selected as VISAA Division II Player of the Year and first-team All-VISAA his senior year, averaging 15.4 points, 11.1 rebounds, 2.2 assists, 2.4 steals and 1.5 blocks. === College recruitment === Brown was consistently rated a three-star prospect and top-15 player in the Virginia class of 2022.{{Cite web |title=Maliq Brown - Duke Blue Devils - Power Forward |url=https://www.on3.com/db/maliq-brown-82077/ |access-date=2024-12-14 |website=On3 |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=Maliq Brown, Duke Blue Devils, Power Forward |url=https://247sports.com/player/maliq-brown-46101768/ |access-date=2024-12-14 |website=247Sports |language=en-US}} He received over a dozen offers to play college basketball before committing to Syracuse over [[Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball|Virginia Tech]], [[NC State Wolfpack men's basketball|NC State]], [[Penn State Nittany Lions basketball|Penn State]] and [[Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball|Georgetown]], and signed a [[National Letter of Intent]] on November 12, 2021.{{Cite web |title=Maliq Brown, Duke Blue Devils, Power Forward |url=https://247sports.com/player/maliq-brown-46101768/ |access-date=2024-12-14 |website=247Sports |language=en-US}} == College career == === Syracuse (2022–2024) === Brown enrolled at [[Syracuse University|Syracuse]] on June 3, 2022 and participated in summer practices.{{Cite web |title=Maliq Brown, Duke Blue Devils, Power Forward |url=https://247sports.com/player/maliq-brown-46101768/ |access-date=2024-12-14 |website=247Sports |language=en-US}} He appeared in 29 games and made seven starts, averaging 20.2 minutes per game.{{Cite web |title=Maliq Brown Career Stats - NCAAM |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/player/stats/_/id/5105337/maliq-brown |access-date=2024-12-14 |website=ESPN |language=en}} Brown contributed a [[double-double]] in a home win over Virginia Tech, and scored a career-high 18 points and four steals in a loss at [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball|Georgia Tech]].{{Cite web |title=Maliq Brown 2022-23 Stats per Game - NCAAM |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/player/gamelog/_/id/5105337/type/mens-college-basketball/year/2023 |access-date=2024-12-19 |website=ESPN |language=en}} As a sophomore, Brown saw a significant uptick in production, starting 18 of 32 games played.{{Cite web |title=Maliq Brown Career Stats - NCAAM |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/player/stats/_/id/5105337/maliq-brown |access-date=2024-12-14 |website=ESPN |language=en}} He achieved the double-double mark four times, including in the [[ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC Tournament]] against NC State.{{Cite web |title=Maliq Brown 2023-24 Stats per Game - NCAAM |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/player/gamelog/_/id/5105337/type/mens-college-basketball/year/2024 |access-date=2024-12-19 |website=ESPN |language=en}} On February 7, 2024, against [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|Louisville]], Brown scored 11 points on 4-for-4 shooting with nine rebounds, five assists, six blocks and five steals.{{Cite web |title=Syracuse 94-92 Louisville (Feb 7, 2024) Box Score |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore/_/gameId/401604175 |access-date=2024-12-19 |website=ESPN |language=en}} He finished the year with 230 rebounds, 29 blocks, and a conference-high 71 steals,{{Cite web |title=Maliq Brown Career Stats - NCAAM |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/player/stats/_/id/5105337/maliq-brown |access-date=2024-12-20 |website=ESPN |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=Men's College Basketball ACC Stat Leaders, 2023-24 Season |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/stats/player/_/season/2024/group/2/table/defensive/sort/avgSteals/dir/desc |access-date=2024-12-20 |website=ESPN |language=en}} and was named to the ACC All-Defensive team, receiving the third-highest number of votes.{{Cite web |title=Duke announces signing of transfer big Maliq Brown |url=https://247sports.com/college/duke/article/duke-announces-signing-of-transfer-big-maliq-brown-230975925/ |access-date=2024-12-19 |website=247Sports |language=en}} === Duke (2024–2026) === Following his sophomore season, Brown announced he would be entering the [[NCAA transfer portal|transfer portal]] on April 2, 2024.{{Cite web |title=Maliq Brown, Duke Blue Devils, Power Forward |url=https://247sports.com/player/maliq-brown-46101768/ |access-date=2024-12-14 |website=247Sports |language=en-US}} He was rated a top-15 [[power forward]] in the portal and around 70th overall.{{Cite web |title=Maliq Brown - Duke Blue Devils - Power Forward |url=https://www.on3.com/db/maliq-brown-82077/ |access-date=2024-12-14 |website=On3 |language=en}} Brown visited [[Duke University|Duke]] on April 18,{{Cite web |last=Wiseman |first=Steve |date=April 18, 2024 |title=Duke basketball is actively looking for transfer portal players. One is visiting campus |url=https://www.newsobserver.com/sports/college/acc/duke/article287774200.html |access-date=2024-12-13 |website=The News & Observer}} and committed to the [[Duke Blue Devils|Blue Devils]] on April 20.{{Cite web |title=Duke men's basketball adds former Syracuse forward Maliq Brown |url=https://www.dukechronicle.com/article/2024/04/duke-mens-basketball-maliq-brown-transfer-portal-jon-scheyer-mark-mitchell-tj-power-sean-stewart |access-date=2024-12-20 |website=The Chronicle |language=en-US}} Brown matched his career-high of five steals in a loss against [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]], the highest output for a Duke player since [[Paolo Banchero]] in 2022.{{Cite web |title=Maliq Brown - 2024-25 - Men's Basketball |url=https://goduke.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/maliq-brown/20758 |access-date=2024-12-14 |website=Duke University |language=en}} In the loss, Brown was kicked in the head by Kansas big man [[Hunter Dickinson]], causing Dickinson to be ejected from the game.{{Cite web |date=2024-11-27 |title=Dickinson ejected for kick as KU survives Duke |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/42634580/kansas-dickinson-ejected-kicking-duke-brown-face |access-date=2024-12-20 |website=ESPN |language=en}} In a win over Notre Dame, Brown suffered a sprained knee, causing him to miss four games.{{Cite web |title=Duke defensive stopper Brown out several weeks |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/43397647/duke-maliq-brown-sprained-knee-miss-extended-period |access-date=2025-01-23 |website=ESPN |language=en}} He then suffered a dislocated shoulder in the Blue Devils' win at [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia]],{{Cite web |date=2025-02-18 |title=Duke Forward Maliq Brown Out Indefinitely After Dislocating Shoulder |url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/duke-forward-maliq-brown-out-indefinitely-dislocating-shoulder-virginia-timeline |access-date=2025-05-11 |website=SI.com |language=en}} and missed another four games before returning in the final game of the regular season in a win at [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]].{{Cite web |title='Welcome back, Maliq': Brown's impact on Duke men's basketball evident in decisive win against North Carolina |url=https://www.dukechronicle.com/article/2025/02/duke-mens-basketball-maliq-brown-impact-defense-passing-north-carolina-jon-scheyer-cooper-flagg-maluach-ngongba |access-date=2025-05-11 |website=The Chronicle |language=en}} In the first game of the ACC Tournament, Brown re-aggravated his shoulder injury, missing the remainder of the tournament and the opening rounds of the [[NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA Tournament]].{{Cite web |date=2025-03-13 |title=Maliq Brown injury update: Duke basketball player exits first half vs Georgia Tech |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/article/maliq-brown-injury-duke-basketball-164748484.html |access-date=2025-05-11 |website=Yahoo Sports |language=en}} He saw limited minutes in the Sweet 16 and Elite Eight, before notching four points, three rebounds and two steals in 15 minutes in a Final Four loss to [[Houston Cougars men's basketball|Houston]].{{Cite web |title=Houston 70-67 Duke (Apr 5, 2025) Box Score |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore/_/gameId/401746080 |access-date=2025-05-11 |website=ESPN |language=en}} On April 23, 2025, the program announced on Instagram that Brown would return for his senior year. Brown scored 10 points against Western Carolina, hitting double-digits for the first time as a Blue Devil.{{Cite web |title=No. 6 Duke Defeats Western Carolina, 95-54, in Home Opener |url=https://goduke.com/news/2025/11/8/mens-basketball-no-6-duke-defeats-western-carolina-95-54-in-home-opener |access-date=2026-01-26 |website=Duke University |language=en}} He notched 12 deflections against Indiana State, and notably deflected a last-second inbound by Florida to clinch Duke's victory.{{Cite web |last=Snyder |first=Anna |title=Duke basketball holds on to defeat Florida in ACC/SEC challenge: Score, highlights |url=https://www.fayobserver.com/story/sports/college/basketball/2025/12/02/duke-basketball-florida-live-updates-score/87506941007/ |access-date=2026-01-26 |website=The Fayetteville Observer |language=en-US}} Brown scored a Duke career-best with 11 points against Lipscomb and matched his career-high again with five steals in a loss to Texas Tech. He started for the first time as a Blue Devil in a win against SMU, and recorded five assists for the first time at Duke against Stanford and Wake Forest.{{Cite web |title=Maliq Brown - 2025-26 - Men's Basketball |url=https://goduke.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/maliq-brown/23103 |access-date=2026-01-26 |website=Duke University |language=en}} == Professional career == On June 24, 2026, the [[San Antonio Spurs]] selected Brown with the 44th overall pick in the [[2026 NBA draft]]. He signed a [[two-way contract]] with Spurs on 3 July, 2026.{{cite web |title=Spurs' four draft picks sign rookie deals|url=https://www.expressnews.com/sports/spurs/article/spurs-four-draft-picks-sign-rookie-deals-22331970.php|website=expressnews.com|date=July 3, 2026}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===College=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2022–23 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2022–23]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2022–23 Syracuse Orange men's basketball team|Syracuse]] | 29 || 7 || 20.2 || '''.698''' || -
